body.text: Terry Denton, children's author and illustrator behind Treehouse series, dies aged 76
In short:
Children's author and illustrator Terry Denton has died at the age of 76, surrounded by his family in Victoria.
Denton had a creative partnership over three decades with author Andy Griffiths, illustrating the Treehouse books, including the 13-Storey Treehouse, which sold more than 10 million copes.
Griffiths said that he and his long-time collaborator had "a match made in heaven".
Australian children's author and illustrator Terry Denton, best known for his work on the popular Treehouse series, has died aged 76.
His literary agency Curtis Brown and publisher Pan Macmillan announced that Denton died surrounded by his family near Melbourne on Monday.

Denton enjoyed a creative partnership spanning three decades with author Andy Griffiths, illustrating the Treehouse books, beginning with the 13-Storey Treehouse, which sold more than 10 million copies worldwide.
He was also known for his Gasp! series, which was adapted for television.
No cause of death was revealed, but Denton had suffered poor health in recent years.
Griffiths paid tribute to his longtime collaborator, describing working and playing with Denton over three decades as "an honour and a pure delight".
"I'll miss him forever, but he's at peace now,"Griffiths said.
"I'm incredibly grateful for his legacy, that we were able to get so much out to the children of Australia and the world."
Over the decades, Denton and Griffiths built global profiles as pranksters, the kind of larrikins that Australia is famous for.
"We were quite different in many ways. It's that difference that makes a creative partnership work … it was a match made in heaven," Griffiths said.
"He had a complete lack of ego. In the books, we were mad at each other all the time, but in real life, it was a very harmonious relationship.
"We would supercharge each other. I would create a structure and he'd come in and throw a spanner in the works.
"We would play with words, play with pictures, play with ideas."
The 78-Storey Treehouse became the fastest-selling book in Australian history when it went on sale in 2016.
Although Griffiths lived just over an hour's drive away from Denton on opposite sides of Port Phillip Bay, he had not seen his co-collaborator for several years.
"As his health declined, he spent all his time with his family, and I totally respected that," he said.
"We always joked that we would go to 13 books with the Treehouse series, and to our surprise we actually did.
"169 stories — 13 times 13 — seemed like the perfect place to stop."
First published in 2011, the 13-Storey Treehouse follows fictional versions of Andy and Terry living in an extraordinary treehouse while battling bizarre distractions as they try to finish a book.
The pair’s attempts to meet a publishing deadline are repeatedly derailed by the treehouse’s bizarre attractions and a series of increasingly chaotic adventures.
Griffiths said he and Denton were "surprised" when their books became popular outside of Australia to some 35 countries.
"The Treehouse was done just for kids in Australia and we had concluded it was too strong a flavour for any other country," he said.
"To our surprise, it went worldwide, tickling the whole world's funny bone, including the UK, Norway, Holland, and South Korea."
Denton won several major awards across his career, including the Children's Book Council of Australia Picture Book of the Year Award in 1986 for Felix and Alexander.
The second youngest of five boys, Denton was born and grew up in Melbourne.
Denton is survived by his wife Kristen, his children Imogen, Eve and Max, and his grandchildren Georgia, Lucy, Charlie, Alfie and Felix.
